question.q: Under Argentina's INV rules, what minimum ageing must a wine have to be labelled 'Reserva', and what for 'Gran Reserva'?
accept: reserva 12 months red and 6 white gran reserva 24 red and 12 white
12 months reds 6 months whites for reserva twice that for gran reserva
reserva one year for reds gran reserva two years for reds
twelve and six months for reserva twenty four and twelve for gran reserva
question.ans: Reserva: 12 months for reds, 6 months for whites and rosés. Gran Reserva: 24 months for reds, 12 months for whites and rosés
question.exp: Argentina legislated these terms (INV Resolution C.32/2011) precisely because they had been decorative, and what the resolution fixes is a stated number of months. Contrast Chile, whose Reserva family hangs on minimum alcohol above the legal floor and on demonstrable oak character rather than any stated ageing period — so 'Reserva' on a Chilean label promises less about elapsed ageing than the same word on an Argentine one. The comparison is a standard trap.
